name: generativepy
role: Python framework for procedural 2D graphics, plots and frame-based animation
notes: 2026-11-15: Triage: assess; plain Python frame generation for mathematical graphics differs from scene-oriented animation tools. Revisit if repeated VCR work establishes a need and Cairo/font dependencies are understood.
2026-11-15: Skill opportunity: further research first; compare a small Python frame-sequence fixture with existing code-first tools before proposing a guide.
2026-11-24: Guide written at skills/generativepy/SKILL.md from the generativepy-frames evidence (shapes and one gradient, PNG frames only).

evidence.result: make_images and out-of-order make_image, 48 frames 320x240 RGBA: 48 distinct hashes, 5 probes match, shuffled equals sequential, rerun byte-identical (digest 4408bd59), middle-frame alpha 0 to 255; Python 3.12.2, pycairo 1.29.2, Cairo 1.18.6, macOS arm64
evidence.scope: Shapes and one gradient, 48 PNG frames 320x240 via pycairo ARGB32; probes, shuffled and rerun byte-identical; no movie, SVG or text; macOS arm64

summary: Python library authors procedural 2D graphics, function plots and frame sequences, with GIF and movie-building routes. Its Python frame model is approachable for data-driven graphics, while movie output depends on additional libraries and it overlaps with other code-first creative tools.
use_when: Create procedural 2D graphics or function plots directly from Python
Render a frame sequence from a Python animation or data source
Use an approachable drawing API rather than building a browser scene
avoid_when: Use Manim for explanatory mathematics with an established animation framework
Use matplotlib for static scientific plots and mature data analysis
Use p5.js when a JavaScript/browser sketch is the natural runtime

assessment.rationale: Official PyPI release 50.0 (2026-08-16) documents procedural 2D graphics, frame-based animation and movie tools under MIT. Movie output depends on optional libraries; the incremental value over existing Python and browser creative tools needs a fixture.
